Popular with tour groups
Aug 2017 • Couples
They have an assortment of banh xeo (a rice "pancake" with sprouts and shrimp, squid and/or meat toppings, rolled in rice paper with herbs, pickled radishes, cucumber and peanut sauce for dipping) and Central Vietnamese dishes like nem lui - a ground and grilled pork sausage that is also rolled in rice paper with various herbs, etc. Also fried rice and fried spring rolls on the menu, which we didn't try. 

Prices are reasonable and service was reasonably efficient, at least until it was time to pay. It's a big place, and the tour buses outside should have been a tip-off that the food wasn't the greatest. I've had banh xeo at many restaurants and know how it should taste, and thought that the banh xeo here was pretty tasteless and the shrimp wasn't as fresh as it should have been. I ended up not finishing the banh xeo as I was worried about getting sick from bad shrimp. The nem lui that we ordered was also quite tasteless. Had to request more rice paper for rolling - 4 sheets wasn't enough for 8 pieces of banh xeo and all the nem lui, too. 

When we asked for the check, we were given the wrong one, which was then replaced with one that had more expensive items than what we ordered, so we had to repeat the process yet again. The third attempt was right. So if you do decide to eat here, and I wouldn't recommend it, check the bill carefully.

This restaurant is also listed on TA as Xeo 75, which I also reviewed negatively.
